diff --git a/kvstore/admin.py b/kvstore/admin.py
index 2817fec..fa77f2c 100644
--- a/kvstore/admin.py
+++ b/kvstore/admin.py
@@ -10,7 +10,7 @@ from .storage import Storage
 
 
 def update_value(storage: Storage, cache: Cache, key: str, value: str) -> None:
-    """Write a new value for key. Note: this only updates the backing
-    store -- a reader whose key is already cached keeps seeing the old
-    value until the cache entry happens to expire (see evictor.py)."""
+    """Write a new value for key, then evict it from the cache so the next
+    read goes to storage and picks up the new value immediately."""
     storage.put(key, value)
+    cache.evict(key)
diff --git a/kvstore/storage.py b/kvstore/storage.py
index 47bb249..ac4954a 100644
--- a/kvstore/storage.py
+++ b/kvstore/storage.py
@@ -1,11 +1,13 @@
 """Backing key-value storage: a small flat-file store.
 
-Storage.get/put persist to a single delimited text file, one "key,value"
-pair per line.
+Storage.get/put persist to a single file, one JSON object per line -- this
+avoids the delimiter-collision bug of the original comma-joined format (a
+key or value containing a comma no longer corrupts a neighboring entry).
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import json
 from pathlib import Path
 
 
@@ -22,9 +24,9 @@ class Storage:
             if not self._path.exists():
                 return None
             for line in self._path.read_text().splitlines():
-                stored_key, _, stored_value = line.partition(",")
-                if stored_key == key:
-                    return stored_value
+                entry = json.loads(line)
+                if entry["key"] == key:
+                    return entry["value"]
             return None
         except OSError as exc:
             raise StorageError(f"failed to read {self._path}: {exc}") from exc
@@ -34,12 +36,15 @@ class Storage:
             existing: dict[str, str] = {}
             if self._path.exists():
                 for line in self._path.read_text().splitlines():
-                    stored_key, _, stored_value = line.partition(",")
-                    existing[stored_key] = stored_value
+                    entry = json.loads(line)
+                    existing[entry["key"]] = entry["value"]
             existing[key] = value
             self._path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
             self._path.write_text(
-                "\n".join(f"{k},{v}" for k, v in existing.items()) + "\n"
+                "\n".join(
+                    json.dumps({"key": k, "value": v}) for k, v in existing.items()
+                )
+                + "\n"
             )
         except OSError as exc:
             raise StorageError(f"failed to write {self._path}: {exc}") from exc

Report your conclusion through the run_control tool before ending your turn: call it with action "affected_verdict" and payload {"phases": [<phase numbers>]} naming every phase that needs work, or with action "no_impact" and payload {"reasoning": "<why the delta needs no artifact changes>"} if none do.

Based on the diff:

- **admin.py**: `update_value` now calls `cache.evict(key)` after `storage.put`, eliminating the previously-documented stale-cache-read window. This removes a known failure mode entirely (no more "reader sees old value until TTL expiry").
- **storage.py**: switches persistence from comma-delimited to JSON-lines. This fixes a delimiter-collision bug, but introduces a new unhandled-exception risk: `json.loads(line)` can raise `json.JSONDecodeError` on any legacy-format or corrupted line, and that exception is *not* caught by the existing `except OSError` handler — so a corrupt/legacy file now crashes the caller instead of raising the module's `StorageError`.

Neither change adds/removes a component or dependency edge (Cache was already a declared collaborator of `admin.update_value`), so the system map itself is unaffected. But the change to what can fail, and how, is exactly what phases 2–4 track: the failure-mode inventory needs the stale-read entry removed and the new uncaught-JSONDecodeError mode added; metric coverage should reflect the new cache-evict operation and the new parse-failure path; alert recommendations should be revisited for the newly-alertable corruption case (and any stale-cache-related alert can be retired).

payload_or_id.title: Storage.put() OS-level write failure
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() (kvstore/storage.py) hits an OSError while writing the backing file (disk full, permission denied, unwritable path, mkdir failure) and raises StorageError. put() reads the whole file, merges the update into an in-memory dict, and writes the whole file back in one write_text() call, so a failure partway through the write can leave the file truncated -- corrupting entries for keys other than the one being written, not just failing the current update. Called only from admin.update_value(), which does not catch it, so the exception propagates to whatever invokes the internal write path (the periodic data-sync job per admin.py's docstring). The affected key's value never updates -- a client of get_value() for that key keeps observing the pre-update value indefinitely -- and if the file was left truncated, subsequent reads of ANY key can fail via storage-malformed-entry-line.

payload_or_id.title: Storage.get() OS-level read failure
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get() (kvstore/storage.py) hits an OSError while reading the backing file (deleted out from under the process, permissions changed, filesystem unmounted) and raises StorageError. Cache.get() does not catch it, so it propagates straight through to api.get_value(), which catches StorageError, increments GET_VALUE_REQUESTS{outcome="error"}, and re-raises to the client -- every cache-miss request for any key fails until the underlying I/O issue is resolved.

payload_or_id.title: Pre-migration comma-format data left in the backing file
payload_or_id.description: This change switched the backing file's line format from comma-delimited (`key,value`) to one JSON object per line, with no migration step and no fallback parser for the old format in Storage.get/put. A data file that still holds pre-migration lines (or is touched by a not-yet-upgraded writer) is silently incompatible; the condition itself produces no symptom by itself -- the next get()/put() call that scans such a line turns it into storage-malformed-entry-line. Worth a pre-deploy/startup check rather than waiting to observe it as a request failure.

payload_or_id.title: Unparseable line in the backing file crashes reads/writes uncaught
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get()/Storage.put() (kvstore/storage.py) call json.loads(line) on every line with no per-line try/except, then index entry["key"]/entry["value"] with no .get(). A line that isn't valid JSON, or is valid JSON missing those fields, raises json.JSONDecodeError or KeyError -- neither is an OSError, so storage.py's `except OSError` does not catch it and it is never wrapped into StorageError. The exception propagates uncaught through Cache.get() and past api.get_value()'s `except StorageError` (which does not match it), reaching the client as an unhandled exception. Because neither the "success" nor "error" label of GET_VALUE_REQUESTS is incremented on this path, this failure is invisible to the service's only existing metric and needs a different detection signal (e.g. an uncaught-exception/process-error signal).

payload_or_id.title: Concurrent Storage.put() calls race and silently drop an update
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() performs a non-atomic read-existing-file / merge-in-memory / write-whole-file-back sequence with no locking. Two overlapping put() calls (e.g. two overlapping runs of the periodic data-sync job) can both read the same starting snapshot and then both write the whole file back; whichever write lands last wins and silently discards the other call's update, with no error raised to either caller -- a client later reading that key observes a value that never reflects the lost update.

payload_or_id.title: Evictor TTL comparison mixes seconds and milliseconds
payload_or_id.description: run_eviction_pass() (kvstore/evictor.py) compares `now = time.time()` (seconds) against `entry.inserted_at_ms` (milliseconds, per Entry in cache.py) with no unit conversion: `now - entry.inserted_at_ms` is always a large negative number, so `> TTL_SECONDS` is never true. No entry is ever evicted by TTL regardless of age or how many eviction passes run -- run_eviction_pass()'s own return value (count removed) is always 0.

payload_or_id.title: In-memory cache grows without bound
payload_or_id.description: Because run_eviction_pass() never removes anything (evictor-ttl-unit-mismatch) and Cache.get() inserts a new in-memory Entry for every distinct key it sees -- including caching None for keys that don't exist in storage -- the cache's `_entries` dict grows monotonically with the number of distinct keys ever requested, for the life of the process. Under sustained unique-key traffic this is unbounded growth with no other mitigation in this codebase; detectable early via a cache-size/RSS trend before it becomes user-visible.

payload_or_id.title: Process OOM/crash from unbounded cache growth
payload_or_id.description: If cache-unbounded-memory-growth is left unaddressed, the process's memory footprint eventually exceeds what the host/container allows and the process is killed or crashes. Every in-flight and subsequent get_value() call fails -- a full outage of the service's only client-facing operation until the process is restarted with a now-empty, cold cache.

payload_or_id.title: Pre-migration comma-format data left in the backing file
payload_or_id.exclusion_reason: A latent precondition with no runtime event to alert on by itself -- best caught by a one-time pre-deploy/startup migration check, not a recurring alert. Its only runtime consequence is captured, and alertable, as fm-storage-malformed-entry-line.
payload_or_id.description: This change switched the backing file's line format from comma-delimited (`key,value`) to one JSON object per line, with no migration step and no fallback parser for the old format in Storage.get/put. A data file that still holds pre-migration lines (or is touched by a not-yet-upgraded writer) is silently incompatible; the condition itself produces no symptom by itself -- the next get()/put() call that scans such a line turns it into fm-storage-malformed-entry-line. Worth a pre-deploy/startup check rather than waiting to observe it as a request failure.

payload_or_id.title: Unparseable line in the backing file crashes reads/writes uncaught
payload_or_id.coverage_reasoning: Bypasses GET_VALUE_REQUESTS entirely (neither outcome label increments), so it is invisible to the only existing metric; needs its own signal (e.g. an uncaught-exception counter around cache.get()/storage.get()/storage.put()) before it can be alerted on.
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get()/Storage.put() (kvstore/storage.py) call json.loads(line) on every line with no per-line try/except, then index entry["key"]/entry["value"] with no .get(). A line that isn't valid JSON, or is valid JSON missing those fields, raises json.JSONDecodeError or KeyError -- neither is an OSError, so storage.py's `except OSError` does not catch it and it is never wrapped into StorageError. The exception propagates uncaught through Cache.get() and past api.get_value()'s `except StorageError` (which does not match it), reaching the client as an unhandled exception. Because neither the "success" nor "error" label of GET_VALUE_REQUESTS is incremented on this path, this failure is invisible to the service's only existing metric and needs a different detection signal.

payload_or_id.title: Concurrent Storage.put() calls race and silently drop an update
payload_or_id.coverage_reasoning: No signal exists today for write attempts, contention, or lost updates on the write path; a write-path metric (e.g. write count, or a version/last-writer check) would be needed before this is alertable.
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() performs a non-atomic read-existing-file / merge-in-memory / write-whole-file-back sequence with no locking. Two overlapping put() calls (e.g. two overlapping runs of the periodic data-sync job) can both read the same starting snapshot and then both write the whole file back; whichever write lands last wins and silently discards the other call's update, with no error raised to either caller -- a client later reading that key observes a value that never reflects the lost update.

payload_or_id.title: Evictor TTL comparison mixes seconds and milliseconds
payload_or_id.exclusion_reason: A static code defect, not a runtime event -- there is nothing to page or ticket on independently of its symptom. The symptom it produces is captured, and alertable via a new metric, as fm-cache-unbounded-memory-growth.
payload_or_id.description: run_eviction_pass() (kvstore/evictor.py) compares `now = time.time()` (seconds) against `entry.inserted_at_ms` (milliseconds, per Entry in cache.py) with no unit conversion: `now - entry.inserted_at_ms` is always a large negative number, so `> TTL_SECONDS` is never true. No entry is ever evicted by TTL regardless of age or how many eviction passes run -- run_eviction_pass()'s own return value (count removed) is always 0.

payload_or_id.title: In-memory cache grows without bound
payload_or_id.coverage_reasoning: No metric exposes cache size or process memory today; a cache-entry-count or RSS gauge is needed to alert on the growth trend before it reaches fm-service-oom-crash.
payload_or_id.description: Because run_eviction_pass() never removes anything (fm-evictor-ttl-unit-mismatch) and Cache.get() inserts a new in-memory Entry for every distinct key it sees -- including caching None for keys that don't exist in storage -- the cache's `_entries` dict grows monotonically with the number of distinct keys ever requested, for the life of the process. Under sustained unique-key traffic this is unbounded growth with no other mitigation in this codebase; detectable early via a cache-size/RSS trend before it becomes user-visible.

payload_or_id.title: Process OOM/crash from unbounded cache growth
payload_or_id.coverage_reasoning: Standard platform-level signal (container restart count / OOMKilled reason) already exists at the orchestrator level; alertable today with an alert rule on that existing infra signal, no new app metric needed.
payload_or_id.description: If fm-cache-unbounded-memory-growth is left unaddressed, the process's memory footprint eventually exceeds what the host/container allows and the process is killed or crashes. Every in-flight and subsequent get_value() call fails -- a full outage of the service's only client-facing operation until the process is restarted with a now-empty, cold cache.

payload_or_id.description: Storage.get()/Storage.put() (kvstore/storage.py) call json.loads(line) on every line with no per-line try/except, then index entry["key"]/entry["value"] with no .get(). A line that isn't valid JSON, or is valid JSON missing those fields, raises json.JSONDecodeError or KeyError -- neither is an OSError, so storage.py's `except OSError` does not catch it and it is never wrapped into StorageError. The exception propagates uncaught through Cache.get() and past api.get_value()'s `except StorageError` (which does not match it), reaching the client as an unhandled exception. Because neither the "success" nor "error" label of GET_VALUE_REQUESTS is incremented on this path, this failure is invisible to the service's only existing metric and needs a different detection signal.

payload_or_id.title: Storage.put() OS-level write failure
payload_or_id.coverage_reasoning: No metric instruments the admin/write path at all today (api.py's counter only covers get_value); a write-outcome signal must be added before this can be alerted on.
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() (kvstore/storage.py) hits an OSError while writing the backing file (disk full, permission denied, unwritable path, mkdir failure) and raises StorageError. put() reads the whole file, merges the update into an in-memory dict, and writes the whole file back in one write_text() call, so a failure partway through the write can leave the file truncated -- corrupting entries for keys other than the one being written, not just failing the current update. payload_or_id.title: Storage.put() OS-level write failure
payload_or_id.coverage_reasoning: No metric instruments the admin/write path at all today (api.py's counter only covers get_value); a write-outcome signal must be added before this can be alerted on.
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() (kvstore/storage.py) hits an OSError while writing the backing file (disk full, permission denied, unwritable path, mkdir failure) and raises StorageError. put() reads the whole file, merges the update into an in-memory dict, and writes the whole file back in one write_text() call, so a failure partway through the write can leave the file truncated -- corrupting entries for keys other than the one being written, not just failing the current update. Called only from admin.update_value(), which does not catch it, so the exception propagates to whatever invokes the internal write path (the periodic data-sync job per admin.py's docstring). The affected key's value never updates -- a client of get_value() for that key keeps observing the pre-update value indefinitely -- and if the file was left truncated, subsequent reads of ANY key can fail via fm-storage-malformed-entry-line.

payload_or_id.description: Storage.get() (kvstore/storage.py) hits an OSError while reading the backing file (deleted out from under the process, permissions changed, filesystem unmounted) and raises StorageError. payload_or_id.exclusion_reason: A latent precondition with no runtime event to alert on by itself -- best caught by a one-time pre-deploy/startup migration check, not a recurring alert. Its only runtime consequence is captured, and alertable, as fm-storage-malformed-entry-line.
payload_or_id.description: This change switched the backing file's line format from comma-delimited (`key,value`) to one JSON object per line, with no migration step and no fallback parser for the old format in Storage.get/put. A data file that still holds pre-migration lines (or is touched by a not-yet-upgraded writer) is silently incompatible; the condition itself produces no symptom by itself -- the next get()/put() call that scans such a line turns it into fm-storage-malformed-entry-line. Worth a pre-deploy/startup check rather than waiting to observe it as a request failure.

payload_or_id.title: Unparseable line in the backing file crashes reads/writes uncaught
payload_or_id.coverage_reasoning: Bypasses GET_VALUE_REQUESTS entirely (neither outcome label increments), so it is invisible to the only existing metric; needs its own signal (e.g. an uncaught-exception counter around cache.get()/storage.get()/storage.put()) before it can be alerted on.
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get()/Storage.put() (kvstore/storage.py) call json.loads(line) on every line with no per-line try/except, then index entry["key"]/entry["value"] with no .get(). A line that isn't valid JSON, or is valid JSON missing those fields, raises json.JSONDecodeError or KeyError -- neither is an OSError, so storage.py's `except OSError` does not catch it and it is never wrapped into StorageError. The exception propagates uncaught through Cache.get() and past api.get_value()'s `except StorageError` (which does not match it), reaching the client as an unhandled exception. Because neither the "success" nor "error" label of GET_VALUE_REQUESTS is incremented on this path, this failure is invisible to the service's only existing metric and needs a different detection signal.

payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() performs a non-atomic read-existing-file / merge-in-memory / write-whole-file-back sequence with no locking. Two overlapping put() calls (e.g. two overlapping runs of the periodic data-sync job) can both read the same starting snapshot and then both write the whole file back; whichever write lands last wins and silently discards the other call's update, with no error raised to either caller -- a client later reading that key observes a value that never reflects the lost update.

payload_or_id.title: Evictor TTL comparison mixes seconds and milliseconds
payload_or_id.exclusion_reason: A static code defect, not a runtime event -- there is nothing to page or ticket on independently of its symptom. The symptom it produces is captured, and alertable via a new metric, as fm-cache-unbounded-memory-growth.
payload_or_id.description: run_eviction_pass() (kvstore/evictor.py) compares `now = time.time()` (seconds) against `entry.inserted_at_ms` (milliseconds, per Entry in cache.py) with no unit conversion: `now - entry.inserted_at_ms` is always a large negative number, so `> TTL_SECONDS` is never true. No entry is ever evicted by TTL regardless of age or how many eviction passes run -- run_eviction_pass()'s own return value (count removed) is always 0.
